text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The military dialogue: Cyprus's purchase of S-300 missiles and a ban on military overflights is the focus of discussions today in Athens between President Clerides and Greek Premier Costas Simitis.
- The state-run Cyprus Broadcasting Corporation will accumulate debts of 45 million pounds in the next five years if nothing is done about its finances soon.
- Clerides is adamant the S-300 will be deployed.
- The Central Bank cuts its rates to commercial banks.
- UN envoy Gustave Feissel expects significant developments in the military dialogue over the next few days.
- Peo trade union criticises the central bank for announcing its intention to deregulate interest rates.
- The U.S. toughens its stance on the S-300 missiles, indicating it will intervene to stop their deployment.
- Infants can remain with their mothers in prison under draft legislation.
- Athens and Nicosia will jointly decide their position on a U.S. proposal to ban overflights.
